passes.summary: Resolved 10 axe incompletes (all colour-contrast on status chips); compared default, CVD (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia, achromatopsia) and forced-colours captures at 1280 for both states; compared 320 and 1280 layouts; scanned copy, headings and controls for judged criteria.

out_of_scope: ARIA snapshot review (snapshots absent from packet)

candidates.title: Sensor status in the Sensors table is conveyed only by dot hue
candidates.description: WCAG 1.4.1 requires that colour is not the only visual means of conveying information. The Status column of the Sensors table shows one small filled dot per sensor: green for pH probe, EC probe and Oxygen probe, orange for Water thermometer and red for Reservoir float. No visible text, icon shape or position differs between the states. In the deuteranopia capture the green and red dots render as near-identical olive; in the achromatopsia capture all five dots are the same mid grey. The same table appears unchanged in the manual-dosing state and at 320 px.
candidates.impact: Colour-blind volunteers, who the context says are on every rota, may be unable to tell which sensor needs attention (top task 3), and may miss that the reservoir float is in a fault state while the reservoir card shows a green 'Topped up' chip.

evidence.detail: five dots: green, green, orange, green, red; no text in Status cells
red (Reservoir float) and green dots both render olive; orange renders mustard
all five dots render as the same grey

factor_notes.frequency: Every sensor row, every visit; the table is the only per-sensor health view.
factor_notes.impact: Fault state of a sensor is not perceivable without hue discrimination.
factor_notes.persistence: Static; does not change with interaction.

candidates.recommendation: Put the status word in the cell (for example 'OK', 'Check', 'Fault'), optionally with distinct icon shapes beside it; keep colour as a secondary cue. Visible text also gives screen-reader users the state without extra ARIA.
candidates.lead_note: split by lead from the auditor candidate per verifier split_required (part 1 of 2)

candidates.title: Sensor status dots are not drawn under forced colours
candidates.description: Under forced colours the Status column of the Sensors table is blank: the background-painted dots are dropped, so no status of any kind remains for users of high-contrast themes.
candidates.impact: Volunteers using a high-contrast or forced-colours theme may see no sensor status at all, including the reservoir float fault.

evidence.detail: Status cells empty: dots not drawn under forced colours

factor_notes.frequency: Every sensor row, every visit; the table is the only per-sensor health view.
factor_notes.impact: Fault state of a sensor is not perceivable without hue discrimination.
factor_notes.persistence: Static; does not change with interaction.

candidates.recommendation: Give the indicator a forced-colours rendering (for example a border or a system-colour fill) or carry the state in visible text.

candidates.title: Automatic dosing switch is not drawn under forced colours
candidates.description: Under forced-colors: active, controls and their selected state should stay visible (A11Y-22). In the forced-colours captures of both the default (on) and manual-dosing (off) states, the switch track and thumb next to 'Automatic nutrient dosing' are not rendered at all; only the label text remains, so neither the control nor its on/off state is visible.
candidates.impact: Volunteers who use a high-contrast or forced-colours mode may not find the control for the critical task (switching dosing to manual) and cannot see whether dosing is automatic from the control itself; the status sentence below remains the only cue.

evidence.detail: no switch drawn right of the label (compare 1280-light-audit.png, where a green on-switch is drawn)
no switch drawn in the off state either

factor_notes.frequency: The only interactive control on the Dosing card.
factor_notes.impact: Control and state invisible in forced colours.

candidates.recommendation: Prefer a native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> or <button aria-pressed>, and inside @media (forced-colors: active) draw the track with a ButtonText border and the thumb/checked fill with Highlight or CanvasText.

candidates.title: Sensors table 'Status' column header is clipped at 320 px
candidates.description: At 320 px content should reflow without loss of information (1.4.10). In the 320 px capture the Sensors table's third column header reads 'Statu', cut at the card's right edge, and the status dots sit at the clipped edge. The scripted reflow check reported no hit, so this may be clipping inside an overflow-hidden card rather than page-level horizontal scrolling.
candidates.impact: Growers checking the bay on a phone may not see the full column header, which compounds the colour-only status column.

evidence.detail: header text visibly truncated to 'Statu' at the card edge

candidates.recommendation: Let the table shrink (smaller cell padding, wrapping headers) or stack rows at narrow widths; avoid overflow: hidden on the card.

needs_human.task: VoiceOver on iPad, journey switch-dosing-to-manual: confirm the switch announces role 'switch', name 'Automatic nutrient dosing' and on/off state, that double-tap toggles it, and that 'Nutrient dosing is now manual...' is announced without moving focus.
Keyboard only: focus the dosing switch, press Space (and Enter) and confirm it toggles, focus stays on it and the state text updates (APG switch pattern). Not probed in this run.

Screen reader: read the Sensors table; confirm it is exposed as a table with column headers and that each Status cell exposes a text state for the coloured dot (otherwise the state is missing for non-sighted users as well).
Screen reader: check the 'Acidity over the last 24 hours' chart has a text alternative or data table conveying the range and trend (it has no y-axis values visually).
Compare screen-reader reading order with the visual order at 320 px and 1280 px (topbar, metric cards, chart, Sensors, Dosing); ARIA snapshots were not in the packet.

Confirm whether readings and 'Last reading' update automatically while the page is open; if they do and updates are presented alongside other content, check there is a way to pause or that the update is essential.
Hover and focus the chart line, metric cards and status dots; if any tooltip appears, confirm it is dismissible with Esc, hoverable and persistent.
Confirm the chart's axis labels are live text, not raster (they kept their colour in forced colours, so the chart may be an image).
Review all instructions and help copy for references that rely on colour, shape or position only (e.g. 'the red dot').
Confirm the nav links 'Readings', 'Sensors', 'Dosing' move focus to their sections on activation.
